messages.subject: Fwd: multiple session-level variables
parts:
Hello Chris,
Thank you very much for your quick response, this previous post is indeed very helpful.
One more layer of complexity to expand on my previous question: my habitat types happen to be nested within sites. i.e. I have 9 sites, and 3 levels of deforestation within each site (one trapping grid for each level of deforestation, that is, 27 grids total). Although the 3 grids within a site were set up far apart to not capture the same rodents, they still are not strictly independent, and this would probably ideally require to introduce a random effect for sites.
The problem is quite similar to repeating the same site in two separate seasons (which we also did)...
Any idea if/how this could be accommodated using oSCR?
Thanks


 
On Thursday, May 14, 2020 at 2:26:56 PM UTC-6, Chris Sutherland wrote:

Hello Mathieu,

 

You can certainly conduct this type of analysis in a very straightforward way using oSCR! You should be able to follow exactly the data formatting described in the vignette/supplement of the oSCR paper in Ecography. The only additional step would be wo add structured density covariates in the spatial data object (the statespace, called ssDF in oSCR). I recently posted code and a description of modeling multi-session density as a function of site level covariates on the oSCR user group. A quick search of the archive will get you to the post (original post was by Clayton Lamb about pooling).

 

Any other questions, feel free to ask (I get immediate notifications for the oSCR list, so am a bit quicker to respond over there).

 

Chris   

 

From: spatialcapt...@googlegroups.com [mailto:spatialcapturerecapture...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Mathieu Pruvot
Sent: Thursday, May 14, 2020 12:48 PM
To: Spatial Capture-Recapture <spatialcapt...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: multiple session-level variables

 

Hello,

I am planning to use oSCR for a rodent study where multiple grids were deployed across different habitat types and seasons, and the primary interest is to test the habitat and seasonal effect on density/group size (much like the example provided in the "multi-session structure" paragraph of the oSCR paper, and the bayesian equivalent in Royle & Converse, 2014). Just wondering if there is a particular way to 1) organize the data and 2) specify the model with multiple session-level variables (in my case, habitat and season)?

Thanks

Mathieu
